mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: original/certified copy -> notarization by a New Zealand notary public -> Apostille by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT). For non-Apostille states: original/certified copy -> notarization -> MFAT authentication -> Consular legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of the destination jurisdiction. The Apostille and Consular Legalization routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: original/certified copy -> notarization by a New Zealand notary public -> Apostille by MFAT. For non-Apostille states: original/certified copy -> notarization -> MFAT authentication -> Consular legalization by the destination Embassy/Consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; no sequential chaining is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Banking
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the proposed New Zealand limited company, attested by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: executed board resolution -> notarization -> MFAT Apostille. For non-Apostille states: executed board resolution -> notarization -> MFAT authentication -> Consular legalization by the destination Embassy/Consulate. The two authentication methodologies are mutually exclusive and cannot be combined in a single chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the proposed New Zealand limited company, certified by the New Zealand Companies Office or a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: certified copy -> notarization -> MFAT Apostille. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a New Zealand licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized officer of a New Zealand registered bank (e.g., ANZ Bank New Zealand, ASB Bank, BNZ, or Westpac New Zealand)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: bank reference letter -> notarization of the authorized signatory's signature -> MFAT Apostille. For non-Apostille states: bank reference letter -> notarization -> MFAT authentication -> Consular legalization by the destination Embassy/Consulate. The Apostille and Consular Legalization routes are parallel and exclusive; sequential chaining is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, authorized representatives, signatories, and beneficial owners must be continuously screened against: (i) the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit targeted financial sanctions lists; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list and sectoral sanctions lists; (iv) the United Kingdom HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List; (v) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; and (vi) politically exposed persons (PEP), adverse media, and regulatory enforcement databases. Screening must be completed before incorporation, repeated upon any ownership or control change, and monitored daily using a certified AML/CFT system. Any match, potential match, or false positive must be escalated to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer within 24 hours and resolved with a documented rationale before proceeding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Company Register online name reservation and incorporation service (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A New Zealand company name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet and must end with 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation such as 'Ltd'. Te Reo Maori names and macrons are permitted. Chinese-language commercial names must be romanized into a phonetically transliterated Latin-script form for the statutory register; only the Latin-script name is legally operative. The four-tier naming convention requires verification of: (1) exact identity with an existing registered name; (2) similarity or phonetic resemblance to existing names; (3) prohibited or restricted expressions requiring ministerial consent; and (4) availability through the Companies Office search facility.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office refuses to reserve a proposed name under sections 22 or 25 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant or its solicitor may file a written reconsideration request under section 24 within 20 working days of the refusal notice. The request must state the original reservation reference, explain why the name is not confusingly similar to existing entries, and provide any ministerial consent or exemption for restricted words. If the Registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand. No automatic extension of the statutory 20-working-day reservation exists; the applicant must file a fresh name reservation with a new distinctive element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under section 200 of the Companies Act 1993, a New Zealand company must maintain a registered office in New Zealand that is a physical address at which legal documents can be served; it cannot be a P.O. Box alone. A virtual office supplying a physical street address and mail-forwarding may satisfy the minimum Companies Office standard, but for this medical-imaging export business, the Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand banks will expect substantive local presence, including a local director, accessible statutory records, a dedicated business telephone and data trail, and evidence of commercial operations. Pure commercial mailboxes are generally rejected by AML/CFT compliance officers and banks because they undermine customer due diligence and transaction monitoring. Accordingly, a virtual office is acceptable only as a secondary service address and not as the principal registered office, principal operational site, or bank account business address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low-to-moderate (approximately 25-35% within the first 18 months) for unannounced physical inspections by the Companies Office or Inland Revenue for a medical device exporter; the probability rises to 70-80% if the registered address is a co-working service address or virtual office. Inspection checklist: (1) confirm a signed lease or occupancy deed; (2) display a durable nameplate with the registered company name; (3) maintain a local director or physical representative accessible during normal business hours; (4) keep the registered office and statutory registers at the declared address; (5) preserve contemporaneous records of medical-device sales, export invoices, equipment descriptions, or product brochures; (6) ensure the business premises shows active administrative operations; and (7) respond to any Companies Office or Inland Revenue correspondence within five working days.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), particularly sections 12 (incorporation), 16-23 (company name restrictions), 24-31 (constitution and default rules), 87-99 (directors), 116-127 (share allotment and registration), 188-198 (registered office and address for service); Companies Regulations 1994; New Zealand Business Number Act 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation (electronic filing through the Companies Register) together with Form 2 - Consent to Act as Director for each proposed director
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement. A company limited by shares may issue shares unpaid, partly paid, or fully paid as determined by the board. No statutory escrow account or capital deposit is required for a standard New Zealand Limited Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the incorporation of the Company be confirmed and that its status as a company limited by shares under the Companies Act 1993 be ratified. (2) That the registered office of the Company be fixed at [Registered Office Address], New Zealand, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified thereof in accordance with section 188 of the Act. (3) That the issue and allotment of 100 ordinary shares of NZD 1.00 each, fully subscribed and paid for by the founding shareholder, be approved, and that the directors be empowered to issue share certificates accordingly. (4) That [Director A], [Director B], and [Director C], having filed their signed consents to act, be and are hereby appointed as directors of the Company. (5) That [Director A] be appointed Managing Director, [Director B] be appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Director C] be appointed Company Secretary, each to hold office until successor appointment. (6) That the directors be authorized to execute all documents and do all acts necessary to obtain an IRD number, GST registration, and all statutory consents required for the manufacture and export of medical imaging devices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability search on the Companies Register. File an online name approval request, which will be automatically checked against identical or confusingly similar existing names and against prohibited or restricted words under sections 20-22 of the Companies Act 1993. A name may be reserved for up to 20 working days. The name must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd'.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (maximum two alternatives)
Name availability search result
Written consent of any professional body or relevant authority if a restricted word is used
Director identification details for the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or objectionability, submit a revised name application through the same online channel; the office fee is not re-levied for a single resubmission within the same application session. If refusal is based on restricted words, supply the consent of the relevant regulatory body.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution, Shareholding Structure, and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Preparatory governance action; final instruments lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Decide whether to adopt a written constitution or to rely on the default rules in the Companies Act 1993. If a constitution is adopted, it must comply with section 27 of the Act. Prepare the shareholding structure, allotment schedule, and addresses for service. Each proposed director must complete and sign Form 2 - Consent to Act as Director, acknowledging duties under the Act.
required_dossiers: Constitution (if adopted, otherwise default rules apply)
Form 2 - Consent to Act as Director for each director
Shareholder register draft with proposed share allotments
Registered office address and address for service in New Zealand
Certificate of name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries incompleteness or inconsistency in the consents or constitution, amend the relevant instrument and resubmit electronically. Typographical defects in the constitution may be cured by a board resolution adopting a corrected version before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Application for Incorporation and Payment of Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the online Form 1 - Application for Incorporation on the Companies Register. Enter the approved company name, registered office, address for service, director details, shareholder details, share structure, and any adopted constitution. Submit electronic consent to act for each director. Pay the statutory filing fee of NZD 200 (approximately USD 120) by credit card or debit from a New Zealand bank account.
required_dossiers: Completed online Form 1 - Application for Incorporation
Electronic Form 2 consent for each director
Company constitution (if any)
Registered office and address for service particulars
Shareholder and share allotment details
Name reservation reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for name-related reasons, the company may be incorporated under a new approved name without a second filing fee, provided the resubmission occurs within the same online transaction. Errors in director or share details may be corrected by filing a Notice of Change after incorporation, with curing delay of one working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Business Number Registrar (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Companies Register automatically issues a Certificate of Incorporation, and the company is assigned a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) under the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016. The certificate and NZBN are available for electronic retrieval from the Companies Register. No further application is required for the NZBN.
required_dossiers: No additional dossiers required; the certificate is auto-generated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains an error in the company name, numbers, or incorporated date, submit an online 'Correction of Register' request to the Companies Office with supporting evidence; corrections are processed within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for IRD Number, GST, and Payroll
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply for a New Zealand IRD number through the Inland Revenue's online tax registration service. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000, or voluntarily where input credits are needed. If employees will be engaged, register as a PAYE employer. Provide the NZBN to link the business tax records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
Company registered office and postal address
Director identification and contact details
Business activity description (medical device manufacturing)
Forecast turnover for GST registration threshold
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue issues a query on the registration, respond within the prescribed period with the NZBN and certificate of incorporation. Any missing identification documents may be resubmitted online. If GST registration is delayed, the effective date may be backdated to the date of first application upon written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Registers and Governance Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Company Secretary, and New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a New Zealand corporate bank account. Establish the statutory registers: share register, director register, and minute book. Issue share certificates under the company seal or electronic equivalent. Schedule the first annual return filing, which must be submitted within 18 months of incorporation and annually thereafter. Appoint an auditor only if required by the constitution or by shareholders holding at least 10 percent of votes.
required_dossiers: Bank account application with certificate of incorporation and director identification
Share register and director register templates
Share certificates for initial allotments
Minute book and first board resolution records
Compliance calendar for annual return and tax filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is not filed on time, file the overdue return online immediately and pay the late filing fee; the Registrar may restore the company to good standing. Missed statutory register entries may be rectified by a board resolution and backdated entries if made in good faith.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Medsafe, New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority, Ministry of Health
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Consent to Distribute a Medical Device (Medical Device Sponsor Licence) under section 33A of the Medicines Act 1981 and Regulation 8 of the Medicines (Medical Devices) Regulations 2002, together with an Export Certificate for Medical Devices issued by Medsafe for consignments to foreign jurisdictions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand with local territorial and regional councils under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Permitted Activity; no formal Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) or Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) is required for the low-impact assembly and testing of portable phased-array ultrasound consoles, provided the facility does not trigger thresholds under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 or the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge of trade waste only with territorial authority approval if volumes exceed 2 cubic metres per day; otherwise comply with regional plan permitted limits. Air emissions: volatile organic compound (VOC) ambient air limit of 1,200 micrograms per cubic metre (30-minute average) under the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004; surface coating processes must use compliant low-VOC solvents. Solid waste: electronic waste containing lead above 0.1 percent or cadmium above 0.01 percent must be classified as hazardous waste and handled under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; transboundary e-waste exports require consent under the Basel Convention. Electromagnetic compatibility and radiofrequency emissions must comply with AS/NZS 60601.1-2 for medical electrical equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification evidenced by a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) with an annual compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004, and an approved Fire Evacuation Scheme issued by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Structural load inspection and compliance certificate issued by the territorial authority following a final inspection by a chartered professional engineer. Workplace clearance issued by WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a general risk assessment, worker engagement procedures, and a hazardous substances inventory if any chemicals are stored above prescribed quantities. Electrical installation certification by a licensed electrician under the Electricity Act 1992.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department – New Zealand (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake; official portal: ird.govt.nz; secure portal: myIR at myir.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned NZ limited company must first be incorporated with the New Zealand Companies Office. After incorporation, apply to the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) for an IRD number via the non-resident company IRD number application process, submitting proof of incorporation, constitutional documents, director and ultimate beneficial owner details, NZ registered office address, and any certified English-language translations. Once the IRD number is issued, activate GST registration in myIR if annual taxable supplies are or are likely to exceed NZD 60,000, or voluntarily if the company makes only zero-rated exports. New Zealand does not issue a separate VAT identification number; the GST number is the IRD number with GST registration status and must be quoted on tax invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An NZ limited company is taxed as a separate entity at the 28% company rate. Closely held companies meeting NZ resident close-company ownership tests may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) treatment, causing current tax items to flow through to shareholders. No US-style check-the-box election exists in New Zealand. Hybrid mismatch and branch mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act 2007 operate mandatorily and restrict deduction/non-inclusion mismatches on hybrid instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST – New Zealand Goods and Services Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of annual taxable supplies made in New Zealand, including remote/digital services supplied to NZ consumers; voluntary GST registration is permitted for exporters and other persons carrying on a taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or transaction-level API filing for GST. E-invoicing via the PEPPOL network is voluntary. Tax invoices, whether paper or electronic, must contain the supplier's GST number, invoice date, supplier and recipient details, description, amount, and GST charged or a zero-rated notation. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR on a periodic (usually monthly or two-monthly) basis.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported by the supplier from New Zealand qualify for GST zero-rating only if the supplier physically exports the goods within 28 days of the time of supply and the goods are not subsequently used or consumed in New Zealand. Services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply may be zero-rated where the service is performed directly for the non-resident and is not supplied to a person in New Zealand or in connection with goods in New Zealand. A Color Doppler Ultrasound Console manufactured in New Zealand and sold to an offshore buyer qualifies for zero-rating when the goods are actually exported under NZ Customs procedures and all export documentation is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged with New Zealand Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank evidence of export proceeds repatriation
Certificate of Origin where required by the destination jurisdiction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits export zero-rating claims strictly. If goods are not exported within 28 days, are diverted to New Zealand use, or the export evidence is incomplete, the supply becomes taxable at 15% GST. Any previously refunded GST or zero-rating benefit is clawed back via amended assessments, with use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 ranging from 20% for reasonable-care and unacceptable-position failures to 100% for abusive tax positions and 150% for evasion. Directors can also incur civil liability, and knowingly false zero-rating documentation may support criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully and freely convertible across both the current account and the capital account. New Zealand maintains no exchange-control legislation, no capital transfer licensing regime, and no administrative filters or approvals for profit remittance, dividend distributions, loan repayments, or repatriation of subscribed capital. The only financial leakage attached to outbound distributions is the Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) imposed under the Income Tax Act 2007 — at the treaty-reduced rate of 15% for fully imputed dividends (5% for AU/NZ treaty investors with a 10% or greater shareholding) — which is a fiscal charge rather than a convertibility restriction. The RBNZ operates an independent free-floating exchange-rate policy, intervening only in exceptional disorderly-market conditions, and the NZD is a G20 deliverable currency settled via continuous linked settlement (CLS). Accordingly, the colour Doppler ultrasound console exporter faces zero statutory convertibility hurdles and may invoice, hold, and reallocate foreign currency without RBNZ notification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil statutory surrender or repatriation obligation. All exchange controls, including the obligation to surrender export proceeds, were repealed in 1984. There is no statutory timeline within which the NZ_LTD exporting entity must return export receivables to New Zealand, and no mandatory conversion ratio of foreign currency earnings into NZD is prescribed. The medical device exporter may retain export proceeds indefinitely in an authorised Foreign Currency Account (FCA), may apply them directly to offshore supplier settlements, or may convert them to NZD at will. The only applicable accounting and tax standard is the requirement to recognise export revenue in NZD equivalent for financial reporting under NZ IFRS and to account for any realised or unrealised FX gains/losses for income tax purposes — neither of which imposes a treasury timing obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Operational Multi-Currency (NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, CNY)
Capital Escrow / Operational Multi-Currency (NZD, USD, EUR, AUD)
Capital Escrow / Operational Multi-Currency (NZD, USD, EUR, JPY) plus Trade Finance and LC line
Capital Escrow / Operational Multi-Currency (NZD, USD, EUR, GB) with Export Finance package
Operational Account (NZD only; foreign currency via arrangement)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary collection/disbursement rails, but Low for primary trade-finance, LC, and statutory treasury infrastructure. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud) may lawfully hold NZD balances and issue NZD domestic account details, provided they operate through an authorised New Zealand reporting entity registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (supervised by the Department of Internal Affairs). However, such EMIs are not registered banks under the Deposit Takers Act 2022; they do not accept deposits in the legal sense, cannot offer documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700), do not participate in the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), and are not CLS members for NZD settlement. Given the ISIC 3250 export model requiring Swift LC and TT/Wire rails, the use of a full-service commercial bank is both legally and operationally mandatory; EMIs are strictly complementary tools for low-value supplier disbursements and expense payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance of directors is not a blanket statutory requirement. All Tier 1 New Zealand banks permit fully remote corporate onboarding for low-risk standard clients — a classification that encompasses a medical imaging exporter (banking_aml_risk_tier: Low_Risk_Standard) — using electronic identity verification (EIV), certified passport extracts, a New Zealand-chartered-accountant or lawyer attestation, and an introduced-banker reference. New Zealand's Electronic Transactions Act 2002 validates digitally executed account mandates and e-signed KYC declarations. However, for the NZ_LTD structure held within an offshore trust or with non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners located in higher-risk jurisdictions, the bank's compliance committee may require a face-to-face or video-interview with the designated director in Auckland or Wellington, alongside notarised board resolutions. In practice, the expedited remote path is available only when (i) the UBO schedule is transparent, (ii) source of wealth is cleanly documented, and (iii) the initial capital injection is via recognised clearing banks; otherwise, one physical or video interview is mandated under the bank's EDD policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) residing in or connected to a FATF-monitored jurisdiction, high-risk jurisdiction, or sanctioned-country nexus (e.g., family trust with discretionary beneficiaries across APAC).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal source-of-wealth report prepared by a New Zealand-incorporated lawyer; full corporate and trust ownership schema showing each intervening layer; certified copies of the trust deed and current beneficiary schedule; two professional bank references from existing financial institutions of the settlor/UBO; and a sworn statutory declaration that no funds or persons are on the New Zealand Sanctions List under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 or the Global Anti-Corruption framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque chain of ownership (non-resident parent company, nominee directors, bearer-share exceptional structures).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organisational chart to ultimate individual shareholder level (vertical chain, no bearer share vehicles), Companies Act 1993 extract with director appointment forms, a letter of explanation of the commercial structure from the NZ auditor, disclosure of any Person with Significant Control (PSC) over the 25% threshold, and a clear narrative that the NZ Ltd entity functions as the substantive local manufacturer of colour Doppler ultrasound consoles with physical premises and payroll.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between expected transaction profile — high-ticket SWIFT LCs and TT wires for medical device export — and the company's stated operating scale or financial capacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master distribution agreements with overseas hospital-supply partners; ISO 13485:2016 and IEC 60601 certificates for the ultrasound console; Medsafe (NZ Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority) conformity certificates; a certified copy of the last 6-month purchase orders; rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast stressing LC settlement amounts; and audited financial statements if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency or high-value outbound wires to jurisdictions that are common transshipment or re-export hubs, raising the risk of diversion or dual-use technology concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bill-of-lading/airway-bill copies evidencing direct shipment to hospital or authorised distributor consignees; due-diligence file on the overseas counterparty (company registration, shareholder list, financial records); Incoterms-based sales contracts with end-user undertakings from the hospital operators; Export control/end-user certification confirming that the phased-array colour Doppler console is a general-purpose medical device not listed on any dual-use or military export schedule of the New Zealand Export Controls regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability or unwillingness of the non-resident directors to provide verified identity for banking onboarding purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled passport copies for every director and UBO; bank-certified 'live-account' reference letters from the director's home jurisdiction bank; remote electronic identity verification (EIV) performed by the NZ bank's licensed provider under the AML/CFT Act; and, where requested, a video conference interview recorded with the individual directors and the bank's compliance officer in compliance with the Privacy Act 2020.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV where upstream aggregation is required) to the NZ bank account of the NZ_LTD, using the bank's unique NZD account IBAN/account number and the wiring narrative structured as: '/INV/ SHARE SUBSCRIPTION — NZD [amount] — Equity contribution' or 'CAPITAL INJECTION — TRADE INVESTMENT'. The remitting account should be the ultimate foreign shareholder's corporate account to preserve source clarity. The injection is matched in the internal reconciliation system against a board special resolution passed per section 51 of the Companies Act 1993, an updated shareholder ledger, and the Companies Office capital filing. For the manufacture of medical devices, the transaction is classified under BOP/BPM6 code 'E1 — Direct Investment Equity Capital', and the Economic Purpose code for bank reporting is '5051 — Direct Investment'. If the capital exceeds NZD 100 million or involves 'sensitive land' or 'significant business assets' within the meaning of the Overseas Investment Act 2005 (unlikely for a standard registration-manufacturer operation), OIO consent is required; for the described entity, no OIO consent is needed. The funds must settle into the Capital Escrow subclass account and then transfer once told to the Operational Account by verified instruction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments for components and inbound raw materials are cleared through two rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account settlements, purchase order advances, and recurring supplier invoices, using standard purpose codes 'Trade in Goods — General Merchandise' and referencing the invoice number and sales agreement; and (ii) Irrevocable Confirmed Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700 / MT710 with MT720 amendments) for high-value or first-transaction imports of ultrasound transducer components and display modules, providing documentary guarantee to the seller. New Zealand-dollar local interbank liquidity is settled through the RBNZ-operated Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) on a real-time gross settlement (RTGS) basis, with the clearing house ensuring finality at the RBNZ. Where USD/EUR disbursements are made directly from the company's Foreign Currency Account, clearing is performed via the bank's offshore correspondent RTGS (e.g., BNZ through National Australia Bank, ANZ through ANZ Group's New York branch), using the applicable local clearing system (CHIPS/Fedwire) to the beneficiary. All export collections may additionally be supported by SWIFT MT400 documentary collection / CAD rails when LC confirmation is not required by the buyer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/CNY, NZD/GBP) under the bank's ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or individual FX-Master Contract, executable at tenors of 1 week to 12 months to fix USD/EUR export receivable conversion prices
FX Swaps (Spot/Forward rollovers) used to manage the liquidity of temporary surplus USD received from LC settlements without creating open FX risk

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS / NZD versus USD/EUR/CNY basis swaps) permitted for long-dated alignment of USD-denominated import payables and trade-finance amortisation under the bank's Treasury ISDA Schedule

Plain-Vanilla FX Options (both call and put on NZD against USD/EUR/CNY), purchased from the dealing bank to establish a floor or ceiling on conversion rates while retaining upside benefit — premium payments are freely remittable

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing offshore non-convertible currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, IDR, VND) of supplier or buyer jurisdictions, permissible under New Zealand law when trade-invoiced positions cannot be materially settled onshore; the NZD itself is a fully deliverable currency and thus no NZD-denominated NDF is required

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the company's annual return date (anniversary of incorporation, unless changed with consent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic late fee; after the Companies Office sends a notice the company has 20 working days to remedy; failure may result in the Registrar removing the company from the register, and directors and the company may be prosecuted with fines up to NZD 10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date: 7 July (paper filers) or 7 October (tax agent filers); alternative balance dates follow the IRD due-date schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 for companies; late payment penalties and use-of-money interest accrue on outstanding tax, with enforcement including seizure of assets if prolonged non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Audit Report (for companies exceeding audit thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (for large and overseas-owned entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance date (if required to file under the Companies Act 1993)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver statutory financial statements to the Companies Office is an offence; directors are liable to fines up to NZD 10,000, and the company may be served with enforcement notices and subsequently removed from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors (internal governance requirement; no external filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, at the date of the annual return or the Board's annual confirmation of registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of registers is an offence under Companies Act 1993 s 211; each director is liable to a fine up to NZD 10,000, and derivatives such as inaccurate share registers may invalidate transfers or delay due diligence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, a company must have audited financial statements if it is 'large' (total assets exceed NZD 33 million or turnover exceeds NZD 10 million) or if it is an overseas-owned company (25%+ ownership) with total assets exceeding NZD 10 million or turnover exceeding NZD 20 million. Issuers and certain charities also require audit irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalent to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB); small and medium-sized profit-oriented entities may apply the XRB's Simplified Mandated Tier 2 framework as appropriate.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate annual UBO filing requirement. Under the Companies Act 1993, share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Shareholders within 10 working days of notification, and the annual return (filed with the Companies Office) confirms the registered shareholders at the annual return date. For AML/CFT purposes, the company must retain beneficial ownership information and update it upon any material change, but no public UBO register exists.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Allotments and Transfers
